conciliatory

catalyst
prerequisite
rival

punctual

dramatize
scrutinize
standardize

Words in Context.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

warning
lullaby
reward

tentative
incidental
reluctant
Words in Context.expl: Matn shifokorlarni 'helpless' (nochor) deb tasvirlash noto'g'ri ekanini, ular faol ravishda davolashni o'zgartirib, tajriba almashganini aytadi. moderated

conventional

Text Structure and Purpose.passage: For decades, textbooks described the Maya city of Tikal as having collapsed suddenly around 900 CE. Recent sediment cores from nearby reservoirs complicate that picture: pollen records indicate that farmers had been abandoning surrounding fields for nearly a century before the city's monuments fell silent. The cores do not reveal why residents left, but they suggest that the "collapse" was less a single catastrophe than a gradual unraveling.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
choices: It presents a long-held view, introduces evidence that challenges that view, and then offers a qualified revision of it.
It describes a historical event, explains the cause of that event in detail, and then predicts the results of future research.
It introduces a scientific method, evaluates its limitations, and then recommends an alternative method.
It summarizes two competing explanations for an event and then argues that neither is supported by evidence.
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Avval eski qarash (to'satdan qulash), keyin yangi dalil (pollen), oxirida ehtiyotkor yangi talqin (asta-sekin). Matn sababini aytmaydi, shuning uchun ikkinchi variant noto'g'ri.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage:
The following text is adapted from a 1911 short story. Mrs. Aldine has just received a letter.
She read it twice, folded it along its old creases, and set it on the mantel beside the clock. Then she took up her sewing again. The needle went in and out, in and out, with a steadiness that anyone watching would have admired; only the thread, pulled a little too tight at every stitch, puckered the hem beyond all mending.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
choices: To suggest that Mrs. Aldine's outward composure conceals a strong reaction to the letter
To show that Mrs. Aldine is more interested in her sewing than in the letter she received
To illustrate Mrs. Aldine's skill as a seamstress despite a distraction
To explain why Mrs. Aldine decides not to respond to the letter
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Tashqaridan xotirjam ko'rinadi, lekin ipni juda qattiq tortib, etakni buzib qo'yadi — bu ichki hayajonni bildiradi. 'Skill' varianti aynan 'puckered beyond all mending' ga zid.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage: Economists often assume that people who receive an unexpected cash windfall will spend it on large purchases. A study of lottery winners in Sweden found something different: most winners kept working, and the typical winner saved or invested the majority of the prize. The researchers note, however, that Swedish lottery prizes are usually modest, so the findings may not apply to recipients of very large sums.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best describes the function of the last sentence in the overall structure of the text?
choices: It acknowledges a limitation on how broadly the study's findings can be applied.
It offers an explanation for why lottery winners in Sweden continued working after winning.
It presents additional evidence that contradicts the economists' assumption about windfalls.
It suggests that the methods the researchers used to study lottery winners were flawed.
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Oxirgi gap natijalar katta summalarga tatbiq etilmasligi mumkinligini aytadi — ya'ni cheklovni tan oladi. U usulni noto'g'ri demaydi.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage: Some ecologists argue that urban coyotes pose a growing threat to pets and should be removed. Wildlife biologist Tamsin Reyes counters that removal programs rarely work: when coyotes are culled, the remaining animals tend to produce larger litters, and new coyotes quickly move into the vacated territory. Reyes instead recommends educating residents to secure garbage and keep small pets indoors at night.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
choices: To present a researcher's objection to a proposed solution and her alternative to it
To explain why coyotes have become increasingly common in urban areas in recent decades
To argue that urban coyotes pose no real threat to pets and should be left entirely alone
To compare the effectiveness of several programs that cities have used to remove coyotes
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Matn olib tashlash taklifini, Reyesning e'tirozini va uning muqobil yechimini ko'rsatadi. Reyes xavf yo'q demaydi — faqat olib tashlash samarasiz deydi.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage: Ecologists have long used the presence of lichens as a rough indicator of clean air, since many lichen species cannot tolerate sulfur dioxide. A 2021 survey of London parks, however, found several sensitive species thriving near busy roads. The researchers point out that sulfur dioxide levels in the city have fallen sharply, while nitrogen pollution from traffic has risen—and that some lichens tolerate, or even benefit from, nitrogen. Lichen surveys, they conclude, now reveal which pollutants are present rather than simply whether the air is clean.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
choices: It describes an established method, reports a finding that seems to undermine that method, and then explains how the method's significance should be reinterpreted.
It introduces a type of air pollution, identifies the main sources of that pollution, and then proposes a practical way of reducing it in cities.
It compares two established methods of measuring air quality and then argues that one of them is considerably more accurate than the other.
It presents a scientific hypothesis about lichens and sulfur dioxide, describes an experiment designed to test it in London, and then reports that the hypothesis was confirmed.
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Avval an'anaviy usul (lishayniklar toza havo belgisi), keyin unga zid ko'ringan topilma, oxirida usulning ma'nosi qayta talqin qilinadi. Usul rad etilmaydi.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage:

They went off down the lane in a noisy cluster, swinging their lunch pails, and not one of them looked back. Cora told herself she was glad of it; that was how it ought to be. Still, she stood in the doorway until the last blue cap had disappeared beyond the mill, and for some time after, as though the lane might yet return something to her.

To illustrate the students' eagerness to leave school and begin working at the mill
To suggest that Cora is disappointed in how her students behaved during the year
To describe the fields and hills surrounding the small school where Cora teaches
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Cora o'ziga 'xursandman' deydi, lekin eshik oldida uzoq turadi — ichki ikkilanish. U bolalarning xatti-harakatidan norozi emas ('that was how it ought to be').

Text Structure and Purpose.passage:

For thirty years Tomas had kept the lighthouse lamp burning, trimming its wick each evening and polishing its lens each morning. When the letter arrived announcing that the light would be automated, he read it twice, folded it carefully, and placed it in the drawer where he kept the logbooks. Then he climbed the stairs, as he did every evening, and lit the lamp. That night, for the first time, he stayed at the top until dawn, watching the beam sweep across water that no longer needed him.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
choices: It presents a character's long-established routine, describes news that threatens that routine, and then depicts the character's quiet response.
It describes a character's decision to leave his long-held job at the lighthouse and then explains in detail the events that led him to make that decision.
It contrasts a character's quiet devotion to his job with the indifference of the officials who hired him many years earlier.
It explains how a lighthouse lamp functions and then describes the new automated technology that is about to replace it.
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Avval 30 yillik odat, keyin xat (avtomatlashtirish), oxirida jim munosabat (tong otguncha qolishi).

Text Structure and Purpose.passage: Economists have long assumed that people who receive an unexpected windfall, such as a lottery prize, will spend it quickly on consumer goods. A study of Swedish lottery winners by Erik Lindqvist and colleagues complicates this picture. Winners did increase their spending, but most of the money was saved or used to pay down debt, and even large prizes had only modest effects on whether winners continued working. The findings suggest that many people treat sudden wealth less as an invitation to consume than as a source of long-term security.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best describes the function of the second sentence in the overall structure of the text?
choices: It introduces research that challenges the assumption described in the first sentence.
It provides an example that supports the assumption described in the first sentence.
It summarizes the methods that economists traditionally used to study windfalls.
It explains why lottery winners in Sweden are unusual compared with winners elsewhere.
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: 1-gap — eski taxmin; 2-gap — 'complicates this picture' — bu taxminni shubha ostiga qo'yuvchi tadqiqotni kiritadi.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage: Architect Diébédo Francis Kéré designed the primary school in Gando, Burkina Faso, using clay bricks made by villagers from local soil. Critics initially dismissed clay as a primitive material unsuited to modern buildings. Kéré, however, stabilized the bricks with a small amount of cement and topped the building with a raised, overhanging roof that shields the walls from rain and allows hot air to escape. The result is a classroom that stays several degrees cooler than concrete buildings nearby, without requiring air conditioning.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
choices: To show how an architect adapted a traditional material to create a building that performs well in its environment
To argue that clay is a better building material than concrete for all modern construction projects, whatever the local climate
To describe the criticism that an architect faced from other architects in Burkina Faso for using clay
To explain why air conditioning remains unavailable in most rural schools and homes in Burkina Faso
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Matn Kéré an'anaviy loyni qanday moslashtirib, issiq iqlimda yaxshi ishlaydigan bino qurganini ko'rsatadi. 'Barcha qurilishlar uchun' — haddan tashqari umumlashtirish.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage: Before the 1960s, most scientists believed that tool use was a uniquely human trait. Then primatologist Jane Goodall observed a chimpanzee in Tanzania stripping leaves from a twig and inserting it into a termite mound to extract insects. Her report forced researchers to reconsider how they defined humans. Today, tool use has been documented in species as varied as crows, octopuses, and sea otters.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence "Her report forced researchers to reconsider how they defined humans" in the text as a whole?
choices: It explains the significance of the observation described in the previous sentence.
It describes the method that Goodall used to observe chimpanzees in the wild.
It introduces a criticism of Goodall's research made by other scientists.
It identifies another species that uses tools in ways similar to Goodall's chimpanzee.
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Oldingi gapda kuzatuv, bu gap esa uning ahamiyatini tushuntiradi (inson ta'rifini qayta ko'rib chiqish).

Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Daryo 'bahslashmaydi', egiladi (bo'ysunish) — lekin oxirida tog'ni zarra-zarra olib ketadi (vaqt o'tib kuchli ta'sir).

Text Structure and Purpose.passage:
The following text is from a novel. Marit has returned to her family's prairie farm after spending a season studying farms in the river valley.

For the first time, it seemed, since the prairie had risen from the ancient inland sea, someone looked upon it not as an obstacle but as a promise. To Marit the long, tawny swells of grass were rich and strong and waiting. She stood at the edge of the field until the wind dried the tears on her face. And the land, which had resisted her father for twenty years, seemed at last to settle under her gaze, as a restless animal grows quiet beneath a familiar hand.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best describes the function of the first sentence in the text as a whole?
choices: It establishes that Marit's hopeful view of the prairie is unprecedented, setting up the final description of how the land seems to respond to her.
It describes the geological origins of the prairie in order to explain why the land had long resisted cultivation by Marit's father.
It suggests that Marit's father never understood the land, a judgment that Marit herself comes to share by the end of the text.
It introduces a tension between Marit's hopes and the land's indifference to them, a tension that remains unresolved and even deepens by the end of the text.
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Birinchi gap: kimdir prairiega birinchi marta 'not as an obstacle but as a promise' deb qaraydi — bu ilgari bo'lmagan qarash. Oxirgi gapda yer 'at last' Maritning nigohi ostida tinchlanadi, ya'ni 1-gap shu yakunga zamin. Geologik kelib chiqish faqat fon, otasining qiyinchiligini tushuntirmaydi. 'Yer befarq, ziddiyat chuqurlashadi' degan variant teskari — yer javob beradi; otasi yerni tushunmagan degan fikr ham matnda yo'q.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage: Many studies of animal cognition test whether individual animals can solve a puzzle, such as retrieving food from a box. Biologist Ipek Kulahci argues that this focus can be misleading for social species. In her experiments with ring-tailed lemurs, the lemurs that solved a feeding puzzle were not necessarily the most skilled problem-solvers; rather, they were the individuals that other group members most often observed. In lemur groups, Kulahci suggests, knowledge spreads along existing social relationships, so the question of which animal solves a problem first may be less informative than the question of which animals are positioned to learn from whom.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
choices: It identifies a common research approach, presents findings that complicate it, and proposes a reframing of the question that approach asks.
It describes a debate between two groups of researchers and then explains why one group's methods are more reliable.
It presents a hypothesis about lemur intelligence, describes an experiment that confirms it, and then considers its possible applications to other species.
It summarizes the history of animal cognition research and argues that recent experiments have made earlier studies obsolete.
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Tuzilma: (1) keng tarqalgan yondashuv — alohida hayvon jumboqni yecha oladimi; (2) Kulahci natijalari buni murakkablashtiradi; (3) savol qayta qo'yiladi — 'kim kimdan o'rganadi'. Ikki guruh olimlar bahsi matnda yo'q. Gipoteza tasdiqlanib, boshqa turlarga qo'llanadi degan variant xato — aksincha yondashuv shubha ostiga olinadi; 'oldingi tadqiqotlar eskirdi' degan variant esa haddan tashqari kuchli.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage: Architectural historians have long credited modernist designers with introducing flat roofs to residential buildings in the early twentieth century. Yet flat roofs had been common for centuries in regions with little rainfall, from North Africa to the American Southwest, where builders used packed earth and timber to create roofs that doubled as outdoor living spaces. What modernists introduced was not the flat roof itself but its use in rainy climates, where it required new waterproofing materials, such as asphalt membranes, that were unavailable to earlier builders.
Text Structure and Purpose.prompt: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
choices: To refine a common claim about the origins of a building feature by distinguishing what was actually new about its modernist use
To argue that modernist designers deliberately copied the flat-roof techniques of builders in North Africa and the American Southwest
To explain why flat roofs are more practical than sloped roofs in regions that receive little rainfall each year
To criticize architectural historians for overlooking the role that asphalt played in the development of modernism
Text Structure and Purpose.expl: Matn keng tarqalgan da'voni ('modernistlar yassi tomni kiritgan') aniqlashtiradi: yangi narsa tomning o'zi emas, uni yomg'irli iqlimda ishlatish edi. Modernistlar ataylab ko'chirgan degan variantga dalil yo'q. Yassi va nishab tomlar amaliyligi taqqoslanmaydi; tarixchilarni asfalt uchun tanqid qilish degan variant haddan tashqari — asfalt faqat tafsilot.

Text Structure and Purpose.passage: Researchers studying bilingual children have noticed that these children sometimes mix words from both languages in a single sentence. For decades, many educators interpreted such mixing as a sign of confusion, evidence that the children could not keep their languages separate. Linguist Fred Genesee's research challenges this view. He found that bilingual children mix languages in systematic ways: they tend to use words from the language their conversation partner speaks best, and they insert words from the other language mainly when they lack an equivalent term. Cross-Text Connections.passage:
Text 1
Does writing notes by hand help students learn more than typing them? In a widely cited 2014 study, Pam Mueller and Daniel Oppenheimer had college students watch recorded lectures while taking notes either on laptops or by hand, and then tested them on the material. Students who took notes on laptops tended to transcribe lectures word for word, while students writing by hand summarized in their own words, and the handwriters performed better on conceptual questions. The study received extensive media coverage, and its findings were soon invoked by instructors and commentators who argued that laptops interfere with the kind of mental processing that deep learning requires.

Text 2
Replication is a routine safeguard in psychology: an effect observed in a single set of experiments with modest numbers of participants may shrink or vanish when the procedure is repeated with more people. When researchers Kayla Morehead, John Dunlosky, and Katherine Rawson repeated Mueller and Oppenheimer's experiments with larger samples, they found that the differences between laptop and handwritten note-takers on conceptual questions were small and not statistically reliable. Such a result does not show that the original effect is absent, only that it is less certain than it first appeared. The researchers caution that the original results, though intriguing, may not justify policies banning laptops from classrooms.
Cross-Text Connections.prompt: Based on the texts, how would Morehead, Dunlosky, and Rawson (Text 2) most likely respond to the findings described in Text 1?
choices: They would argue that the findings did not hold up clearly enough in follow-up research to support firm conclusions.
They would argue that the findings show that laptops should be removed from classrooms to improve students' learning.
They would argue that students who transcribe lectures word for word tend to perform better than students who summarize.
They would argue that the original study did not measure how students performed on conceptual questions at all.
Cross-Text Connections.expl: Text 2: katta namunada farq kichik va statistik ishonchsiz chiqqan — asl natijalar qat'iy xulosa uchun yetarli emas. Noutbuklarni sinfdan olib tashlash kerak degan variant teskari — ular aynan bunday taqiqni oqlamaydi deyishadi. So'zma-so'z yozganlar yaxshiroq degan da'vo yo'q, asl tadqiqot esa konseptual savollarni o'lchagan.

Cross-Text Connections.passage:
Text 1
The shift from foraging to farming, which began roughly 10,000 years ago in Southwest Asia and arose independently in several other regions, is usually portrayed as a triumph of human ingenuity. By domesticating plants such as wheat, rice, and maize and animals such as goats and cattle, early farmers produced food surpluses that allowed populations to grow, permanent villages to form, and eventually complex societies, with their specialized crafts, writing, and cities, to emerge. From this perspective, early farmers were better off than the hunter-gatherers who came before them, having traded an uncertain life of constant movement for a more secure and settled existence.

Text 2
Skeletal remains tell a more complicated story. By comparing bones and teeth from burial sites dated to just before and just after the local adoption of agriculture, anthropologists have found that in many regions the transition to farming coincided with a decline in average height and an increase in dental cavities and signs of nutritional stress, such as defects in tooth enamel that form during periods of childhood hunger. Farming may have supported larger populations, but individual farmers often ate less varied diets, heavy in starchy grains, and worked longer hours than their foraging ancestors. A growing population, in other words, is not the same as a population of healthier individuals.
Cross-Text Connections.prompt: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the perspective described in Text 1?
choices: By acknowledging that agriculture enabled population growth while questioning whether it improved the well-being of individual farmers
By denying that the adoption of agriculture ever produced the food surpluses that allowed larger populations and complex societies to emerge
By arguing that populations of hunter-gatherers grew more rapidly than early farming populations did in most regions
By suggesting that the decline in average height among early farmers resulted from factors unrelated to their diets
Cross-Text Connections.expl: Text 2 'Farming may have supported larger populations' deb o'sishni tan oladi, lekin suyak dalillari alohida dehqonlar ahvoli yomonlashganini ko'rsatadi. Ortiqcha oziq-ovqatni butunlay inkor etgan variant xato. Bo'y pasayishi ovqatga bog'liq emas degan variant ham teskari — Text 2 aynan ovqat kamroq xilma-xil bo'lganini aytadi; ovchilar aholisi tezroq o'sgani haqida esa gap yo'q.

Cross-Text Connections.passage:
Text 1
Sofonisba Anguissola, born in Cremona around 1532, was among the first women painters of the Italian Renaissance to achieve international fame. She is also notable for the unusual number of self-portraits she produced over her long career, ranging from small miniatures to larger canvases. Scholars have often read these works dismissively: either as expressions of personal vanity or as simple practice pieces produced because she lacked access to other models, such as the hired sitters that male artists of the period routinely studied in workshops. On either reading, the self-portraits reveal little about Anguissola's ambitions as a professional artist and deserve less attention than her other works.

Text 2
Art historian Mary Garrard argues that Anguissola's self-portraits were a deliberate professional strategy. As a woman, Anguissola could not easily obtain public commissions, so she used self-portraits, which were collected by aristocrats as curiosities, to circulate her image and demonstrate her skill to potential patrons. A small portrait could travel far beyond Cremona, passing among courts and collectors who might never meet the painter herself. In several of the self-portraits she depicts herself painting or playing an instrument, emphasizing her accomplishments rather than her appearance. Details that might seem incidental thus become, on this reading, elements of a carefully managed public identity designed to attract the patronage her career depended on.
Cross-Text Connections.prompt: Based on the texts, how would Garrard (Text 2) most likely respond to the scholars' interpretation in Text 1?
choices: By arguing that it overlooks how the self-portraits served Anguissola's efforts to advance her career
By agreeing that the self-portraits were mainly practice pieces but disputing that they reflect vanity
By claiming that Anguissola painted self-portraits only after she had received many public commissions
By suggesting that aristocrats collected the self-portraits because of their technical flaws
Cross-Text Connections.expl: Garrard: avtoportretlar ongli kasbiy strategiya — o'z mahoratini homiylarga ko'rsatish. Text 1 buni e'tibordan chetda qoldiradi. B: 'mashq' degan qismga ham qo'shilmaydi. C: aksincha, u buyurtma ololmagan. D: 'kamchiliklar' tufayli emas, qiziqarli narsa sifatida yig'ilgan.

Central Ideas and Details.passage:
The following text is adapted from a 1905 novel. Hester has recently moved from the countryside to work in a city shop.
The city did not frighten her, as her mother had predicted it would. What unsettled Hester was something smaller: that no one on the crowded pavements ever looked at anyone else. At home a stranger on the road was an event, to be greeted and discussed for days. Here a thousand strangers passed her every morning, and she began to feel that she, too, was becoming invisible.

choices: Hester is troubled less by the size of the city than by the way its residents ignore one another.

Hester is frightened by the large crowds she encounters each morning on her way to work.

Central Ideas and Details.passage: Geologist Anvar Tursunov studies caves in the Baysun Mountains, where layered mineral deposits called flowstones record changes in rainfall. Because each layer's chemistry reflects the water that formed it, Tursunov can reconstruct wet and dry periods going back 40,000 years. His records show that the region's climate shifted abruptly several times, with some transitions from wet to dry conditions taking less than a century—far faster than earlier models had assumed.
Central Ideas and Details.prompt: According to the text, what did Tursunov's research reveal?
choices: Some major climate shifts in the region occurred more rapidly than had been previously thought.
The chemistry of the flowstones varies little from one layer to the next over thousands of years.
The region's climate has remained dry for most of the past 40,000 years, with few major changes.
Earlier climate models of the region relied mainly on data collected from similar flowstones.
Central Ideas and Details.expl: Oxirgi gap: ba'zi o'zgarishlar 100 yildan kam vaqtda bo'lgan — avvalgi modellar taxmin qilganidan tezroq.

Central Ideas and Details.passage: When the city of Bogotá closed more than 100 kilometers of streets to cars every Sunday, officials expected the program to encourage exercise. Surveys found that it did, but they also revealed an effect planners had not anticipated: residents of wealthy and poor neighborhoods, who rarely shared public spaces during the week, mingled on the car-free routes. Researchers now cite the program as an example of how transportation policy can shape social life as well as health.
Central Ideas and Details.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
choices: A program intended mainly to promote exercise also had a significant social effect.
Closing streets to cars is the most effective way for cities to improve residents' health.
Residents of wealthy neighborhoods in Bogotá exercise more than residents of poor neighborhoods.
Officials in Bogotá designed the car-free program to reduce divisions between neighborhoods.
Central Ideas and Details.expl: Dastur jismoniy mashq uchun edi, lekin kutilmagan ijtimoiy natija berdi. Oxirgi variant xato: rasmiylar buni rejalashtirmagan ('had not anticipated').

Central Ideas and Details.passage:
The following text is adapted from a 1920 essay. The writer is describing an old bookshop.
The proprietor knew the location of every volume, though no catalogue existed and the shelves obeyed no system a customer could discern. Ask him for a book on beekeeping and he would disappear between two leaning stacks, returning minutes later with exactly the volume you wanted—and, more often than not, a second one you had not known you needed.
Central Ideas and Details.prompt: Based on the text, what is true about the proprietor?
choices: He has a detailed knowledge of his shop's disorganized collection.
He has recently created a detailed catalogue of the books in his shop.
He specializes in selling old and rare books about beekeeping.
He is reluctant to help customers who ask for particular books.
Central Ideas and Details.expl: Katalog yo'q, tizim ko'rinmaydi, lekin u har bir kitob joyini biladi — tartibsiz to'plamni juda yaxshi biladi.

Central Ideas and Details.passage: Coral reefs are often described as "rainforests of the sea," and like rainforests they are commonly thought to depend on stable conditions. But marine biologist Tevita Fonua's surveys of reefs around Tonga suggest a more complicated picture. Reefs that had experienced moderate storm damage every few years supported more coral species than either reefs that were rarely disturbed or reefs battered by frequent severe storms. Fonua proposes that occasional disturbance prevents a few fast-growing species from crowding out others.
Central Ideas and Details.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
choices: Research suggests that a moderate level of disturbance may help maintain coral diversity on reefs.
Coral reefs around Tonga contain a greater variety of species than most tropical rainforests do.
Frequent severe storms are the main threat to the survival of coral reefs and their species around Tonga.
Fast-growing coral species are more resistant to storm damage than other coral species are.
Central Ideas and Details.expl: Asosiy g'oya: o'rtacha bezovtalik tur xilma-xilligini saqlaydi. Kuchli bo'ronlar tafsilot, asosiy fikr emas.

Central Ideas and Details.passage:
The following text is adapted from a 1921 essay about the writer's grandfather.
He distrusted any machine he could not take apart. The new tractor stood in the barn for a full season while he studied it, bolt by bolt, filling a notebook with drawings; only when he could have rebuilt it blindfolded did he consent to drive it into the field. My father thought this a waste of a good summer. My grandfather thought it the only honest way to own a thing.
Central Ideas and Details.prompt: Based on the text, how does the grandfather's view of the tractor differ from the father's?
choices: The grandfather believes that truly owning the tractor requires understanding how it works, whereas the father sees that effort as unnecessary.
The grandfather believes the tractor is poorly made and unreliable, whereas the father thinks it will last for many years.
The grandfather wants to sell the old tractor to a neighbor, whereas the father wants to keep it and use it on the farm.
The grandfather prefers to do most of the farm work by hand, whereas the father prefers to rely on modern machines such as the family's new tractor.
Central Ideas and Details.expl: Bobo mashinani to'liq tushunishni 'yagona halol egalik' deb biladi; ota esa buni yozni isrof qilish deb hisoblaydi.

Grandfather never threw anything away. The shed behind his house held jars of bent nails, coils of wire, the handles of shovels whose blades had long since rusted through. As a child, Leila had thought it was simply clutter. It was only after the storm, when half the fences on the road were down and the hardware store in town had been closed for a week, that she watched him walk into the shed and return, again and again, with exactly what each neighbor needed.

choices: Leila comes to see that her grandfather's habit of saving things, which she once dismissed, has real value.

Central Ideas and Details.passage: For decades, the standard account held that the domestication of horses began on the grasslands of Kazakhstan around 5,500 years ago, where the Botai people left behind thousands of horse bones and pottery containing traces of mare's milk. A 2018 genetic study complicated this account. Researchers found that Botai horses were not ancestors of modern domestic horses but of Przewalski's horses, a wild population. Modern domestic horses, it turned out, descend from a different lineage that spread across Eurasia roughly 4,200 years ago.
Central Ideas and Details.prompt: According to the text, what did the 2018 genetic study reveal?
choices: The horses associated with the Botai people are not the ancestors of today's domestic horses.
The Botai people did not keep horses themselves but hunted wild horses and drank mare's milk.
Przewalski's horses are descended from modern domestic horses that escaped and became wild.
Horse domestication began in Kazakhstan considerably more recently than 4,200 years ago.
Central Ideas and Details.expl: Tadqiqot: Botai otlari zamonaviy uy otlarining emas, Prjevalskiy otlarining ajdodi. Boshqa variantlar matnga zid.

Central Ideas and Details.passage: Urban planners once measured the success of a city street mainly by how quickly cars could move along it. Writer and activist Jane Jacobs challenged this view in the 1960s. She argued that the most successful streets were those with a constant mix of people using them for different purposes at different times of day: shoppers in the morning, office workers at lunch, diners in the evening. Such streets, she wrote, were not only livelier but safer, because they were always watched by many eyes.
Central Ideas and Details.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
choices: Jacobs argued that streets should be judged by how well they support varied human activity rather than by traffic flow.
Jacobs believed that cars should be banned from city streets so that pedestrians could use them freely at all times of day.
Urban planners in the 1960s were mainly concerned with making city streets safer for pedestrians.
Jacobs found that office workers were the most important users of city streets in most neighborhoods.
Central Ideas and Details.expl: Jacobs mashinalar tezligi o'rniga ko'chaning turli odamlar tomonidan ishlatilishini muvaffaqiyat mezoni deb bilgan.

Central Ideas and Details.passage: Octopuses have about 500 million neurons, but roughly two-thirds of them are located not in the brain but in the arms. Studies by neuroscientist Binyamin Hochner and others suggest that each arm can process touch and taste information and coordinate simple movements on its own, even when severed from the body. The brain appears to issue general commands, such as "reach toward that shell," while the arms work out many of the details independently.
Central Ideas and Details.prompt: Based on the text, which choice best describes how an octopus controls its arms?
choices: The brain gives broad instructions, and the arms handle many specifics of movement themselves.
The brain controls every movement of each arm directly, even the smallest ones.
The arms act on their own and largely ignore the signals they receive from the brain.
Each arm contains a separate brain that is larger and more complex than the central brain of the octopus.
Central Ideas and Details.expl: Miya umumiy buyruq beradi, qo'llar tafsilotlarni o'zi hal qiladi.

The following text is adapted from an original essay.

We speak of "finding time" as though hours were coins that had rolled beneath the furniture, waiting only to be discovered. But no one has ever found an hour. Time is not found; it is taken from one thing and given to another. The person who says she has no time to read has not been robbed of reading hours by some thief. She has spent them, perhaps wisely, on something else, and the honest question is not where the time went but whether it went where she would have chosen.

Central Ideas and Details.expl: Vaqt 'topilmaydi', bir ishdan olinib boshqasiga beriladi — asosiy savol: vaqt biz tanlagan joyga ketdimi.

Central Ideas and Details.passage: Glaciologists have long used the retreat of mountain glaciers as a straightforward indicator of rising temperatures. A recent study complicates this picture. Examining glaciers in the Himalayas, the researchers found that glaciers covered by thick layers of rock debris retreated far more slowly than bare glaciers at the same elevation, because the debris insulated the ice beneath it from the sun. Yet satellite measurements showed that many debris-covered glaciers were thinning almost as quickly as bare ones, losing ice from their surfaces even though their fronts barely moved.
Central Ideas and Details.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
choices: Because debris-covered glaciers can lose substantial ice without retreating much, the position of a glacier's front may be an unreliable measure of its response to warming.
Because rock debris shields glacial ice from sunlight, debris-covered glaciers in the Himalayas are largely protected from the effects of rising temperatures and lose little ice overall.
Satellite measurements of glacier thickness are less reliable than ground-based observations of where a glacier's front is located each year.
Rock debris absorbs heat from the sun and therefore causes Himalayan glaciers to thin more quickly than they would if they were bare.
Central Ideas and Details.expl: Asosiy g'oya: qoplangan muzliklar sekin chekinadi, lekin deyarli bir xil tezlikda yupqalashadi — demak muzlik chetining joylashuvi isishni o'lchashda ishonchsiz ko'rsatkich. 'Qoplama muzni himoya qiladi, kam muz yo'qotiladi' degan variantni yupqalanish rad etadi. 'Qoplama yupqalanishni tezlashtiradi' degan variant ham xato — matn 'almost as quickly' deydi; usullar aniqligi esa umuman taqqoslanmaydi.

Central Ideas and Details.passage:
The following text is from a novel set in a small farming town in the 1920s. Nell has come back to the town after many years away.

Everyone saw her arrive, because it was evening. The sun had gone down, but the sky still held its color. It was the hour for sitting on porches along the road, the hour for hearing things and saying things. All day these people had been hands and backs and shoulders, bent to the fields and the mill, and nobody had asked what they thought. But now the whistle had blown and the foreman had gone home, and the evening belonged to them. They felt tall and full of words, masters of every story that passed along the road.

They have gathered on the porches specifically to welcome Nell back to town after her many years away.
The colors of the evening sky remind them of the beauty of the countryside surrounding their town.
They have rested on their porches throughout the day and are finally recovering from their exhaustion.

Central Ideas and Details.passage: Microbiologist Lynn Margulis spent years defending the idea that mitochondria, the structures that produce energy inside plant and animal cells, originated as free-living bacteria that were engulfed by other cells. Critics found the idea implausible. Margulis pointed to features that mitochondria share with bacteria: they have their own DNA arranged in a circular loop, they reproduce by dividing in two independently of the cell around them, and their internal machinery for building proteins resembles that of bacteria rather than that of the cells they inhabit.
Central Ideas and Details.prompt: Based on the text, what is the purpose of the features Margulis identified?
choices: They served as evidence that mitochondria share an ancestry with bacteria.
They explained how mitochondria produce energy for the cells that contain them.
They showed that mitochondria can survive outside of plant and animal cells today.
They demonstrated that bacteria evolved from structures similar to mitochondria.

B: energiya ishlab chiqarish mexanizmi tushuntirilmaydi. C: bugun tashqarida yashashi aytilmagan — 'independently' faqat bo'linishga tegishli. D: yo'nalish teskari.

Central Ideas and Details.passage: Urban historian Kenneth Jackson argues that the spread of American suburbs after 1945 was not simply the result of consumer preference. Federal mortgage insurance programs, he notes, strongly favored newly built single-family houses over the renovation of older urban apartments, and the interstate highway system made long commutes practical. While many families certainly desired suburban homes, Jackson contends that government policy made that choice far cheaper and easier than the alternatives, shaping preferences as much as responding to them.
Central Ideas and Details.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
choices: Jackson argues that government policies played a major role in encouraging postwar suburban growth.
Jackson argues that most American families did not actually want to live in suburbs after 1945.
Jackson argues that the interstate highway system was built primarily to serve suburban commuters.
Jackson argues that federal mortgage programs made urban apartments more affordable than suburban houses.
Central Ideas and Details.expl: Asosiy g'oya: siyosat (ipoteka, yo'llar) shahar atrofi o'sishini kuchli rag'batlantirgan. B: 'many families certainly desired' — aksincha. C: magistral maqsadi aytilmaydi. D: teskari — dasturlar yangi uylarni qo'llagan.

Central Ideas and Details.passage: Although rainforests are often described as the 'lungs of the planet,' ecologist Yadvinder Malhi points out that a mature rainforest absorbs roughly as much carbon dioxide through photosynthesis as it releases through the respiration of its plants, animals, and microbes. Such a forest is valuable not because it adds oxygen or removes carbon from the atmosphere on balance, Malhi argues, but because it stores enormous amounts of carbon in its trees and soil, carbon that would be released if the forest were cleared or burned.
Central Ideas and Details.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
choices: The climate importance of a mature rainforest lies mainly in the carbon it holds rather than in any net removal of carbon from the air.
Because mature rainforests release more carbon dioxide than they absorb through photosynthesis, they contribute to rather than slow climate change.
Rainforests produce most of the oxygen that animals depend on, which is why they are often called the lungs of the planet.
Because mature rainforests absorb little carbon on balance, clearing them would have little effect on atmospheric carbon.
Central Ideas and Details.expl: Malhi: yetuk o'rmon yutgan va chiqargan CO2 taxminan teng ('roughly as much'), qadri esa daraxt va tuproqda saqlangan uglerodda. 'Yutganidan ko'p chiqaradi' degan variant matnga zid. 'Kesish kam ta'sir qiladi' degan variant teskari — kesilsa saqlangan uglerod chiqadi; kislorod haqidagi variant esa matn rad etgan 'o'pka' tasvirini takrorlaydi.

Central Ideas and Details.passage: Sociologist Mark Granovetter's influential 1973 study examined how people in a Boston suburb found their jobs. Granovetter expected that close friends and family members would be the most useful sources of job information. Instead, he found that people more often learned about the jobs they eventually took from acquaintances they saw only occasionally. Granovetter reasoned that close contacts tend to know the same people and hear the same news, whereas acquaintances move in different social circles and can therefore pass along information a person would not otherwise encounter.
Central Ideas and Details.prompt: According to the text, why did acquaintances prove especially useful to job seekers?
choices: They had access to information that differed from what job seekers' close contacts could provide.
They were more willing than close friends and family members to personally recommend job seekers to employers.
They were more likely than family members to work in the industries job seekers wanted to enter.
They saw job seekers only occasionally and therefore had fewer obligations to other people.
Central Ideas and Details.expl: Tanishlar boshqa ijtimoiy doiralarda yuradi, shuning uchun yaqinlar bilmagan yangi ma'lumotni yetkazadi. Ish beruvchiga tavsiya qilishga tayyorlik yoki kerakli sohada ishlash haqida matnda gap yo'q. 'Kam uchrashgani uchun majburiyatlari kam' degan variant ham matnda aytilmagan sabab.

Command of Evidence (Textual).passage: Marine ecologist Ruth Okafor hypothesizes that parrotfish, which scrape algae off coral, help reefs recover after bleaching events by clearing space where new coral larvae can settle. To test the idea, Okafor compared bleached reef sections from which parrotfish had been excluded by cages with nearby bleached sections left open to parrotfish.
Command of Evidence (Textual).prompt: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Okafor's hypothesis?
choices: Three years after bleaching, the open sections had significantly more young coral colonies than the caged sections did.
Three years after bleaching, the caged sections had significantly more young coral colonies than the open sections did.
Parrotfish were seen scraping algae more often on healthy reef sections than on reef sections that had been bleached.
Three years after bleaching, the open and caged sections had about the same number of young coral colonies.
Command of Evidence (Textual).expl: Gipoteza: parrotfish joy ochib, yangi korallar o'sishiga yordam beradi. Ochiq qismda yosh korallar ko'proq bo'lsa — to'g'ridan-to'g'ri tasdiq. Suv o'tlari bir xil bo'lsa, aksincha gipotezani zaiflashtiradi.

Command of Evidence (Textual).passage: Some historians have argued that the spread of clocks in eighteenth-century England changed how workers experienced time, making them more conscious of hours and minutes. Historian Priya Nair suggests that this shift happened more gradually than those historians claim, and that many rural workers continued to organize their days by tasks and daylight well into the nineteenth century.
Command of Evidence (Textual).prompt: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Nair's claim?
choices: Diaries kept by agricultural laborers in the 1820s describe their workdays mainly in terms of completed chores and sunrise and sunset, rarely mentioning clock times.
Diaries kept by agricultural laborers in the 1760s describe their workdays mainly in terms of clock times, often noting the exact hour at which each task began.
Records show that clocks became common in the homes of wealthy families in eighteenth-century England, often placed in the entrance hall where guests could see them.
Factory owners in the 1780s posted rules requiring workers to arrive at a set hour, and they fined workers who arrived even a few minutes after the bell had rung.
Command of Evidence (Textual).expl: Nair: qishloq ishchilari XIX asrgacha vazifa va kun yorug'ligi bo'yicha yashagan. 1820-yillardagi kundaliklar aynan shuni ko'rsatadi. Zavod jarimalari esa aksincha soatga e'tiborni ko'rsatadi.

Command of Evidence (Textual).passage: Psychologist Mei Lin hypothesized that people remember information better when they explain it aloud to someone else than when they simply reread it, even if the listener asks no questions. In her study, participants studied a passage and then either reread it or explained it to a silent listener; a week later, all participants took the same recall test.
Command of Evidence (Textual).prompt: Which finding from Lin's study, if true, would most strongly support her hypothesis?
choices: Participants who explained the passage to a silent listener recalled substantially more of it than did participants who reread it.
Participants who reread the passage recalled about as much of it as did participants who explained it aloud to a silent listener in the study.
Participants who explained the passage to a listener who asked questions recalled more than those whose listener stayed silent.
Participants who explained the passage to a silent listener said the task felt harder and more tiring than simply rereading it.
Command of Evidence (Textual).expl: Gipoteza eslab qolish haqida — tushuntirgan guruh ko'proq eslab qolgani bevosita tasdiqlaydi. Yoqtirish yoki vaqt esa eslab qolishni o'lchamaydi.

Command of Evidence (Textual).expl: Da'vo ikki qismli: yorqinlik + yolg'izlik. Faqat birinchi iqtibosda ikkalasi bor: minglab yonayotgan derazalar va har birining ortida yolg'iz yuz.

Monarchs whose antennae were painted to block light cues flew in the correct direction just as reliably as did the monarchs whose antennae had been painted with clear paint.
Monarchs that were kept in darkness for several days lost weight more quickly than monarchs kept under a normal daily cycle of light and dark.
Monarchs can detect the scent of milkweed plants from a distance of several meters using sensitive receptors located along their antennae.
Command of Evidence (Textual).expl: Gipoteza: vaqtni mo'ylovlardagi soat kuzatadi. Mo'ylovlarga yorug'lik tushmasa yo'nalish buziladi — to'g'ridan-to'g'ri dalil. Qolganlari vaqt/yo'nalish bilan bog'liq emas.

Command of Evidence (Textual).passage: "The Silent Orchard" is an original novel about a farming family. In the novel, the narrator suggests that the family's eldest son, Pavel, values his father's approval more than he admits: ______

"The orchard produced more apples that year than it had in a decade, though no one in the family, not even Pavel's father, could say exactly why it had done so."
Command of Evidence (Textual).expl: Da'vo: Pavel tan olmaydi, lekin otasining roziligini qadrlaydi. To'g'ri iqtibosda u 'no longer cared' deydi, ammo har kechqurun otasi qatorlarni aylanib bosh irg'amaguncha darvoza oldida kutadi — ikkala qism ham bor. Otasidan hech qachon fikr so'ramagani haqidagi iqtibos aksincha befarqlikni ko'rsatadi; otasi maqtamasligi yoki hosil haqidagi iqtiboslar Pavelning his-tuyg'usini ko'rsatmaydi.

Firelight talk mostly concerned practical matters such as land and food, while daytime talk consisted largely of stories about other people, many of whom were not present.

About 80% of daytime talk and about 80% of firelight talk consisted of stories about people, many of whom were not present at the time the stories were told.
Command of Evidence (Textual).expl: Da'vo: olov atrofidagi suhbat alohida ijtimoiy vazifaga ega. To'g'ri variant kunduzgi (amaliy: yer, ovqat) va kechki (80% hikoyalar) suhbatni solishtirib, kechqurun madaniy bilim uzatilishini ko'rsatadi. Mazmunni teskari bergan variant kunduzgi suhbatni alohida qilib qo'yadi; 'ikkalasida ham 80% hikoya' degan variant esa farq yo'qligini ko'rsatadi. Faqat davomiylik va ishtirokchilar soni mazmun haqida gapirmaydi.

choices: After otters returned to a stretch of coast where they had been absent, urchin numbers there fell sharply and kelp cover increased within a few years.

Command of Evidence (Textual).expl: Sabab zanjiri: otter qaytadi → dengiz kirpilari kamayadi → kelp ko'payadi. To'g'ri variant aynan shu ketma-ketlikni ko'rsatadi. Kirpilar soni o'zgarmay kelp ko'paygan degan variant zanjirning o'rta bo'g'inini uzadi. Otterlar asosan qisqichbaqa va mollyuska yegani yoki iliqroq suv haqidagi variant boshqa sababga ishora qiladi.

Command of Evidence (Textual).expl: Dittmar: savdo talabi muhimroq. To'g'ri variant savdo markazlarini o'xshash kattalikdagi diniy markazlar bilan solishtirib, 1500-yilgacha pres savdo shaharlarida ko'proq bo'lganini ko'rsatadi. 'Diniy markazlarda ko'proq' degan variant aksincha raqib qarashni qo'llaydi; diniy kitoblar ko'p bosilgani ham Cherkov qarashiga mos. Pres qanchalik tez tarqalgani esa sababni ko'rsatmaydi.

Users on most of the websites studied addressed older strangers formally more often than they addressed younger strangers formally, whatever the site's usual norms.

Command of Evidence (Textual).expl: Gipoteza: tanlov yoshga emas, sayt me'yoriga bog'liq. To'g'ri variantda bir xil yoshdagi odamlarga o'yin forumida norasmiy, rasmiy murojaat ustun yangiliklar saytida esa rasmiy murojaat qilingan — yosh o'zgarmagan, me'yor o'zgargan va tanlov ham o'zgargan. Command of Evidence (Textual).passage: The Glass Ballroom is a 1908 novel by Eleanor Whitcombe. "The sunlight lay on the lawn and the gravel walks, and Lily, pausing on the terrace, felt the charm of the scene."

Command of Evidence (Textual).expl: Taklif: to'qlik signali vaqt oladi, shuning uchun sekin yeganlar kamroq yeydi. Command of Evidence (Textual).expl: Da'vo: dengizchilar millatidan qat'i nazar o'zaro birdam bo'lgan, o'z ofitserlariga qarshi. Command of Evidence (Textual).expl: Taklif: yomg'irdan hosil bo'lgan muz qatlami vazn kamayishiga sabab. choices: Even though pollinators could not reach any of the flowers, nectar volume in sun-exposed plants fell from 2.3 to 0.9 microliters over the day, while it stayed near 2.5 microliters in shaded plants.
In the morning, before the heat of the day, shaded plants and sun-exposed plants had similar nectar volumes, averaging 2.4 and 2.3 microliters per flower, respectively, in Ahmadi's study.
Shaded plants had slightly more nectar per flower at midday (2.6 microliters) than they did in the morning (2.4 microliters), and they still had 2.5 microliters per flower in the evening.

Even though pollinators could not reach any of the flowers, nectar volume fell over the course of the day in both groups, from about 2.4 to 0.9 microliters in shaded and sun-exposed plants alike by evening.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).expl: Changlatuvchilar hech bir gulga yeta olmagan, demak kamayish issiqlikdan. Faqat quyoshdagi o'simliklarda kamayish va soyadagilarda barqarorlik — xulosani to'liq qo'llab-quvvatlaydi.

Command of Evidence (Quantitative).passage: Urban planner Sofia Marchetti studied bike-share programs in two cities. She noticed that ridership in City B, which had built protected bike lanes before 2018, grew steadily every year, whereas ridership in City A, which added protected lanes only in 2021, was more volatile. Marchetti suggests that protected lanes help a program keep riders even when outside conditions change.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).prompt: Which choice best describes data from the graph that support Marchetti's suggestion?
choices: In 2020, trips per day fell from 14,000 to 9,000 in City A but rose from 9,000 to 11,000 in City B.
City A had more trips per day than City B in every year shown, including 2020, when it had 9,000.
Trips per day in City A reached 18,000 in 2022, higher than in any other year shown in the graph.
In 2020, trips per day rose from 9,000 to 11,000 in City A but fell from 14,000 to 9,000 in City B.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).expl: Taklif: himoyalangan yo'laklar sharoit o'zgarganda ham chavandozlarni saqlaydi. 2020-yilda yo'laklarni kech qurgan shaharda qatnovlar 14 000 dan 9 000 ga tushgan, yo'laklari oldindan bor shaharda esa 9 000 dan 11 000 ga oshgan. Raqamlarni shaharlar o'rtasida almashtirgan variant grafikka zid; 'har yili ko'proq qatnov' degan variant 2020-yilda noto'g'ri, 2022-yil rekordi esa barqarorlik haqida emas.

Command of Evidence (Quantitative).passage: Agronomist Kwame Asante compared farm plots planted with cover crops (plants grown between main crops to protect soil) with plots left bare. At the start of the growing season, both types of plots had similar soil moisture. Asante concluded that cover crops help soil retain moisture as the season becomes hotter and drier: ______
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).prompt: Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the statement?
choices: by August, soil moisture had fallen to 23% in plots with cover crops but to 15% in plots without them.
in April, soil moisture was 31% in plots with cover crops and 32% in plots that had no cover crops.
by August, soil moisture had fallen to 15% in plots with cover crops but only to 23% in plots without them.
soil moisture in plots with cover crops decreased every month from April to August, falling from 31% to 23%.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).expl: Xulosa: issiq va quruq davrda qoplama ekinlar namlikni saqlaydi. Aprelda namlik deyarli teng edi, avgustga kelib esa qoplamali uchastkalarda 23%, qoplamasizlarda 15% — farq aynan shuni ko'rsatadi. Raqamlarni almashtirgan variant grafikka zid; aprel holati haqidagi variant faqat boshlang'ich tenglikni, faqat qoplamali uchastkalar haqidagi variant esa taqqoslashsiz pasayishni ko'rsatadi.

Command of Evidence (Quantitative).passage: Researchers tested whether planting strips of wildflowers next to crop fields increases the number of native bees visiting the crops. They counted bee visits to blueberry flowers in fields with and without wildflower strips over three years. They concluded that the benefit of the strips grew over time as bee populations became established.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).prompt: Which choice best describes data from the table that support the researchers' conclusion?
choices: The difference in bee visits between fields with strips and fields without strips increased from Year 1 to Year 3.
Fields without wildflower strips received between 18 and 19 bee visits per 100 flowers in every year of the study.
In Year 1, fields with strips received more bee visits than fields without strips, 22 visits compared with 18 visits.
The difference in bee visits between fields with strips and fields without strips decreased from Year 1 to Year 3.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).expl: Xulosa: foyda vaqt o'tgani sari ortgan. Farq 1-yilda 4 (22 va 18), 2-yilda 13, 3-yilda 25 — farqning o'sishi aynan shuni ko'rsatadi. 'Farq kamaygan' degan variant jadvalga zid; faqat 1-yilni yoki faqat gul yo'laklari yo'q dalalarni aytgan variantlar vaqt bo'yicha o'zgarishni ko'rsatmaydi.

Command of Evidence (Quantitative).passage: A team of economists studied whether offering free public transit passes changes how older adults travel. They compared adults aged 60 to 64, who were not eligible for free passes, with adults aged 65 to 69, who were eligible. The team claims that free passes mainly led people to make new trips rather than replacing trips they previously made by car.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).prompt: Which choice best describes data from the table that support the team's claim?
choices: Adults aged 65 to 69 made many more transit trips per week than adults aged 60 to 64, but only slightly fewer car trips.
Adults aged 60 to 64 made more car trips per week than transit trips, averaging 8.2 car trips and just 1.1 transit trips.
Adults aged 65 to 69 made many more car trips per week than adults aged 60 to 64, but only slightly more transit trips.
Adults in both age groups made a similar number of walking trips per week, about 4, and roughly 8 car trips per week each.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).expl: Da'vo: bepul chiptalar yangi sayohatlar qo'shgan, mashina sayohatlarini almashtirmagan. 65–69 yoshlilarda transport 1.1 dan 3.4 ga (+2.3) oshgan, mashina esa atigi 8.2 dan 7.9 ga kamaygan. 'Mashina sayohatlari ancha ko'p' degan variant jadvalga zid; piyoda yurish yoki faqat 60–64 yoshlilar haqidagi variantlar ikki guruh farqini ko'rsatmaydi.

Command of Evidence (Quantitative).passage: Ecologists measured the survival of oak seedlings planted in a forest under three conditions: in open areas, under shrubs, and in areas surrounded by fences that kept out deer. A student claims that, in this forest, protection from deer mattered more for seedling survival than shade did.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).prompt: Which choice best describes data from the graph that support the student's claim?
choices: Survival after three years was far higher for fenced seedlings than for seedlings under shrubs, which survived only slightly better than seedlings in open areas.
Survival after three years was far higher for seedlings under shrubs than for fenced seedlings, which survived only slightly better than seedlings in open areas.
Survival declined each year for seedlings in all three conditions, although seedlings in open areas had the lowest survival rate in every year of the study.
More than half of the seedlings under shrubs and in open areas survived the first year, but fewer than a quarter of each group survived through the third year.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).expl: Da'vo: bug'udan himoya soyadan muhimroq. 3-yilda: to'siqli 71%, buta ostida 24%, ochiq 18% — to'siq katta farq beradi, soya esa kichik.

Command of Evidence (Quantitative).passage: A city library began offering evening hours in 2021. A report claims that the change attracted new visitors rather than simply shifting existing visitors to later times.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).prompt: Which choice best describes data from the graph that support the report's claim?
choices: Daytime visits stayed about the same after 2021, while total visits rose because of the added evening visits.
Evening visits rose each year after they were introduced, from about 6,000 in 2021 to about 13,000 in 2023.
Daytime visits fell sharply after 2021, while total visits stayed about the same despite the added evening visits.
Total visits in 2020 were slightly lower than total visits in 2019, before evening hours were introduced.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).expl: Agar tashrif buyuruvchilar shunchaki kechga ko'chganda edi, kunduzgi tashriflar kamayardi. Kunduzgi ~ 40 da qolgan, jami esa oshgan — yangi tashrif buyuruvchilar.

Command of Evidence (Quantitative).passage: Scientists compared the average body length of a species of lizard on islands with different numbers of predator species. They hypothesized that lizards evolve longer legs relative to body length on islands with more predators, since longer legs allow faster running.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).prompt: Which choice best describes data from the table that support the scientists' hypothesis?
choices: Relative leg length increased as the number of predator species increased, while body length stayed about the same.
Body length increased as the number of predator species increased, while relative leg length stayed about the same.
Lizards on Island D, which had six predator species, had the greatest average body length, 55.8 millimeters.
Average body length varied by less than 2 millimeters across the four islands, from 54.2 to 55.8 millimeters.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).expl: Gipoteza oyoq nisbiy uzunligi yirtqichlar soni bilan ortadi. Jadvalda 0.41 → 0.47 → 0.52 → 0.58, tana uzunligi deyarli bir xil.

Command of Evidence (Quantitative).passage: Economists studied whether a four-day workweek affects productivity. At several companies, some teams switched to a four-day week while others kept a five-day week. The economists argue that the shorter week did not reduce output: teams working four days completed roughly as many projects per month as they had before the change, even though teams that stayed on a five-day week also improved slightly.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).prompt: Which choice best describes data from the graph that support the economists' argument?
choices: Four-day teams completed 18 projects per month before the change and 18 after, while five-day teams went from 17 to 19.
Five-day teams completed an average of 19 projects per month after the change, compared with 18 projects per month for four-day teams.
Before the change, four-day teams completed an average of 18 projects per month, while five-day teams completed an average of 17.
Both four-day and five-day teams completed fewer projects per month on average after the change than they had before it.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).expl: Da'vo: 4 kunlik hafta natijani kamaytirmagan (18 → 18), 5 kunlikdagilar ozgina yaxshilangan (17 → 19). A aynan shuni ko'rsatadi. B: grafikka mos (19 > 18), lekin da'voni qo'llamaydi — aksincha. C: 18 > 17 to'g'ri, lekin o'zgarish haqida emas. D: noto'g'ri.

Command of Evidence (Quantitative).passage: Ornithologist Ana Paula Silva tracked the arrival dates of a migratory songbird at its breeding site over five years. She claims that birds that spent the winter farther south arrived later in spring, but that the gap between the two groups narrowed over the study period.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).prompt: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to support Silva's claim?
choices: In year 1, southern-wintering birds arrived 12 days after northern-wintering birds, while in year 5 they arrived 5 days after them.
Northern-wintering birds arrived at the breeding site on April 16 in year 1 and on April 17 in year 5, one day later than before.
In every year of the study, southern-wintering birds arrived at the breeding site on or after April 22, later than northern-wintering birds.
Southern-wintering birds arrived at the breeding site on April 28 in year 1 and on April 22 in year 3, six days earlier than before.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).expl: Da'vo ikki qismli: (1) janubdagilar kechroq keladi, (2) farq qisqargan. Jadval: 1-yil 28-aprel − 16-aprel = 12 kun; 5-yil 22-aprel − 17-aprel = 5 kun. Faqat A ikkalasini ham ko'rsatadi. B: shimoliylar aslida 1 kun kechroq kelgan (16 → 17). C: 'after April 20' to'g'ri, lekin farq qisqarishini ko'rsatmaydi. D: faqat bitta guruh.

Command of Evidence (Quantitative).passage: A city introduced a congestion charge for cars entering its downtown area in 2019. A transportation analyst claims that the charge reduced car traffic downtown without reducing the total number of people traveling there, because many former drivers switched to buses.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).prompt: Which choice best describes data from the graph that support the analyst's claim?
choices: From 2018 to 2020, daily car trips downtown fell from about 60,000 to about 40,000, while daily bus trips rose from about 30,000 to about 50,000.
Daily bus trips downtown reached about 50,000 in 2020, more than in any other year shown, and remained near that level in 2021.
Daily car trips downtown held steady at about 60,000 in 2017 and 2018 and then fell to about 40,000 in 2020, where they remained in 2021.
From 2018 to 2020, daily car trips downtown fell from about 60,000 to about 40,000, while daily bus trips also fell, from about 50,000 to about 30,000.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).expl: Da'vo: mashina kamaygan, lekin umumiy sayohat kamaymagan (odamlar avtobusga o'tgan). 2018–2020: mashina 60 000 dan 40 000 ga tushgan, avtobus 30 000 dan 50 000 ga oshgan — jami taxminan 90 000 saqlangan. 'Avtobus ham kamaygan' degan variant grafikka zid. Faqat avtobus yoki faqat mashina haqidagi variantlar da'voning bir qismini ko'rsatadi, xolos.

Command of Evidence (Quantitative).passage: Researchers compared how quickly three species of coral recovered after a marine heat wave bleached a reef. A student claims that the species that was most severely bleached was not the species that recovered most slowly.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).prompt: Which choice best describes data from the table that support the student's claim?

Species Y had a lower percentage of bleached colonies than species X did, and a higher percentage of its colonies recovered than species Z's.
Species X had the highest percentage of bleached colonies, and species Y had the highest percentage of bleached colonies recovered after one year.
Species Z had a higher percentage of bleached colonies than species Y did but a lower percentage of bleached colonies than species X did.

Command of Evidence (Quantitative).passage: Psychologist Tomás Ruiz surveyed students about how many hours per night they slept and asked them to rate their mood. He claims that the relationship between sleep and mood is not simply linear: mood improved sharply as sleep increased up to about seven hours but changed very little beyond that point.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).prompt: Which choice best describes data from the graph that support Ruiz's claim?
