Command of Evidence (Quantitative).passage: An agricultural researcher tested whether intercropping (growing two crops in the same field) affects yields. She planted maize alone, beans alone, and maize with beans together. She concludes that intercropping produced more total food per hectare than either crop alone, even though each individual crop yielded less when grown with the other.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).prompt: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to support the researcher's conclusion?
choices: Intercropped fields produced 4.1 tons of maize and 1.6 tons of beans per hectare, a total of 5.7 tons, compared with 5.0 tons for maize alone and 2.2 tons for beans alone.
Intercropped fields produced 4.1 tons of maize per hectare, 0.9 tons less than the 5.0 tons per hectare produced by fields in which maize was grown alone.
Intercropped fields produced 4.1 tons of maize and 1.6 tons of beans per hectare, a total of 5.7 tons, compared with 6.0 tons for maize alone and 2.2 tons for beans alone.
Beans grown alone produced 2.2 tons per hectare, more than the 1.6 tons per hectare produced by beans grown with maize, and maize alone produced 5.0 tons per hectare.
Command of Evidence (Quantitative).expl: Xulosa: jami hosil (4.1 + 1.6 = 5.7 tonna) har bir ekinning alohida hosilidan (5.0 va 2.2) ko'p. To'g'ri javob buni to'liq ko'rsatadi. 'Makka alohida 6.0 tonna' degan variant jadvalga zid (aslida 5.0) va unda 5.7 kamroq bo'lib chiqadi. Faqat makka yoki faqat loviya kamaygani haqidagi variantlar 'jami ko'proq' qismini ko'rsatmaydi.

Inferences.passage: Archaeologists excavating a Bronze Age settlement found hundreds of loom weights, the clay objects used to hold threads taut during weaving. Yet the settlement's soil contained almost no traces of the flax or wool fibers that weavers would have used, and no remains of sheep were found among the animal bones at the site. Because loom weights are heavy and were rarely transported far, the archaeologists concluded that ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: the settlement's weavers likely obtained their fibers from somewhere other than the settlement itself.
the loom weights found at the settlement were probably used for some purpose other than weaving.
the settlement's residents probably did not wear any woven clothing, despite owning many looms.
sheep must have been raised at the settlement even though no traces of their bones have been preserved there.
Inferences.expl: To'quvchilik joyida bo'lgan (og'ir toshlar uzoqqa tashilmagan), lekin tola va qo'y yo'q — demak tolani boshqa joydan olishgan. 'Bones not preserved' matn dalillariga zid taxmin.

Inferences.passage: In many bird species, females prefer males with elaborate songs. Researchers studying a species of warbler found that males raised in noisy urban areas sang simpler songs than rural males did, but urban females did not show a weaker preference for complex songs when tested in quiet conditions. If complex songs continue to signal male quality to females, ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: urban males may be at a disadvantage in attracting mates compared with rural males.
urban females will likely begin to prefer simpler songs within a few generations.
rural males will likely begin singing simpler songs to compete with urban males.
noise in cities has no effect at all on which males are chosen as mates by females.
Inferences.expl: Shahar erkaklari soddaroq kuylaydi, urg'ochilar esa baribir murakkab kuyni afzal ko'radi — demak shahar erkaklari juft topishda noqulay holatda bo'lishi mumkin.

Inferences.passage: A company tested two versions of its website. Version A displayed prices including tax, while version B displayed prices before tax and added tax at checkout. Visitors to version B added more items to their carts, but a larger share of them abandoned their carts at checkout. The company's analysts noted that total sales were nearly identical for the two versions, suggesting that ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: the additional items placed in carts on version B were largely offset by the higher rate at which those carts were abandoned.
visitors to version A placed more items in their carts than visitors to version B did, even before any of the carts were abandoned.
displaying prices before tax has no effect whatsoever on how shoppers behave at any stage of the online purchasing process.
most shoppers do not notice whether the prices displayed on a website include tax, even when they reach the checkout page.
Inferences.expl: Soliqsiz narx ko'rsatilgan versiyada savatga ko'proq narsa qo'shildi, lekin ko'proq savat tashlab ketildi, umumiy savdo esa deyarli bir xil — demak biri ikkinchisini qoplagan. 'Umuman ta'sir qilmaydi' degan variant xato, chunki xaridorlar xatti-harakati o'zgargan. Soliqli versiyada savatga ko'proq qo'shilgan degan variant matnga zid; xaridorlar soliqni sezmaydi degan variant esa tashlab ketish oshganiga to'g'ri kelmaydi.

Inferences.passage: Glaciologists drilling into an Antarctic ice sheet found a layer of volcanic ash about 1,000 meters below the surface. The ash's chemistry matches that of a known eruption in New Zealand, which other evidence dates to roughly 25,000 years ago. Because ice layers accumulate from the surface downward over time, the ice directly above the ash layer ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: must have formed less than roughly 25,000 years ago.
must have formed more than roughly 25,000 years ago.
was likely formed from ash deposited by the same eruption.
is probably thicker than the ice directly below the ash layer.
Inferences.expl: Muz yuqoridan pastga to'planadi, demak kul ustidagi muz kuldan keyin, ya'ni 25 000 yildan kamroq vaqt oldin hosil bo'lgan.

Inferences.passage: In many desert plants, a type of photosynthesis called CAM allows leaves to open their pores only at night, when cooler air reduces water loss. Botanist Salma Haddad found that one shrub species switches to CAM only during droughts, using ordinary daytime photosynthesis when water is plentiful. Because ordinary photosynthesis supports faster growth but loses more water, Haddad's finding suggests that the shrub ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: trades rapid growth for water conservation only when conditions make conservation necessary.
grows more quickly during droughts than it does in periods when water is readily available.
is unable to survive in regions where droughts are common, since it cannot conserve water.
uses CAM at all times, conserving water even when doing so is not necessary for its survival.
Inferences.expl: Suv ko'p bo'lsa tez o'sish (oddiy fotosintez), qurg'oqchilikda suvni tejash (CAM) — ya'ni o'simlik faqat zarur bo'lganda tezlikni tejashga almashtiradi.

Inferences.passage: Historians studying medieval trade have relied heavily on surviving merchant contracts, most of which were drawn up by notaries in large port cities such as Genoa and Venice. Economic historian Nadia Sorensen notes, however, that small inland traders rarely used notaries, often sealing agreements orally or with brief informal notes that were seldom preserved. If Sorensen is correct, reconstructions of medieval commerce based mainly on notarial contracts ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: may overrepresent the activity of large coastal merchants relative to that of small inland traders.
are likely to underestimate the importance of large port cities such as Genoa and Venice to medieval trade.
should be replaced by studies of inland traders' oral agreements, which were carefully preserved.
demonstrate that small inland traders were more numerous than coastal merchants.
Inferences.expl: Saqlangan shartnomalar asosan port shaharlaridagi notariuslardan — kichik ichki savdogarlar deyarli qayd etilmagan. Demak manbalar yirik qirg'oq savdogarlarini ortiqcha aks ettiradi.

Inferences.passage: Most of the ancient Roman concrete that survives today contains small white lumps of lime. Scholars long assumed these lumps were signs of careless mixing. But a team led by Admir Masic found that when cracks form in the concrete and water seeps in, the lime lumps dissolve and recrystallize as calcium carbonate, filling the cracks. This finding suggests that ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: features once regarded as flaws in Roman concrete may have contributed to its durability.
Roman builders deliberately added water to their concrete in order to make it stronger.
modern concrete contains considerably more lime than Roman concrete did in antiquity.
the lime lumps in Roman concrete are signs of careless mixing that weakened the material.
Inferences.expl: Nuqson deb hisoblangan ohak bo'laklari yoriqlarni to'ldiradi — demak ular mustahkamlikka hissa qo'shgan bo'lishi mumkin.

Inferences.passage: In a series of experiments, psychologist Ellen Langer gave residents of a nursing home a houseplant. Residents in one group were told that they were responsible for watering and caring for the plant and could make choices about their daily schedules; residents in a second group were told that the staff would care for the plant and make those decisions for them. Eighteen months later, residents in the first group were more active and alert than those in the second group. If the groups were otherwise similar, the results suggest that ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: having a sense of control over one's environment may benefit the well-being of older adults.
caring for houseplants is more beneficial than any other activity for nursing home residents.
nursing home staff are generally unable to care for plants properly.
residents in the second group disliked the plants they were given.
Inferences.expl: Guruhlar orasidagi farq — nazorat va tanlov imkoniyati. Demak nazorat hissi foydali bo'lishi mumkin. B haddan tashqari keskin.

Inferences.passage: Glaciers in the Himalayas supply meltwater to rivers that serve hundreds of millions of people. As the climate warms, the glaciers are melting faster, which in the short term increases the flow of water in these rivers. However, the glaciers are also shrinking, and once they lose enough mass, less ice will be available to melt each summer. Thus, communities that currently benefit from increased river flow should expect that ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: the flow of water from glacial melt will eventually decline.
rivers in the region will continue to rise indefinitely.
the Himalayan glaciers will begin growing again once rivers reach their peak flow.
the amount of rainfall in the region will decrease.
Inferences.expl: Hozir erish ko'paydi, lekin muzliklar kichraysa, eriydigan muz kamayadi — oqim oxir-oqibat kamayadi.

Inferences.passage: The Voynich manuscript, a fifteenth-century book written in an unknown script, has resisted decades of attempts at decipherment. Some researchers have suggested it is an elaborate hoax containing meaningless text. However, statistical analyses show that the frequency of its words follows the same pattern found in natural languages, in which a few words appear very often and most words appear rarely. Because a forger working in the fifteenth century would have been unlikely to know about such patterns, these analyses suggest that ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: the manuscript is more likely to contain meaningful language than random text.
the manuscript was written in a language that is still spoken today.
the manuscript was produced much later than the fifteenth century.
statistical analysis will soon allow researchers to fully translate the manuscript.
Inferences.expl: Tabiiy tillarga xos statistik naqsh bor, soxtakor buni bilmagan bo'lardi — demak matn ma'noli bo'lishi ehtimoli yuqori. D haddan oshiq.

Inferences.passage: Tardigrades, microscopic animals that can survive extreme dehydration, produce a protein called Dsup that binds to their DNA. When researchers inserted the gene for Dsup into human cells grown in a laboratory, the cells suffered about 40% less DNA damage from X-rays than unaltered cells did. This result suggests that, in tardigrades, Dsup likely ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: helps protect the animals' DNA from damage.
allows the animals to survive without water permanently.
is produced only when the animals are exposed to X-rays.
causes the animals' cells to divide more rapidly.
Inferences.expl: Dsup inson hujayralarida DNK zararlanishini kamaytirdi — tardigradlarda ham DNK ni himoya qilishi ehtimoli bor.

Inferences.passage: In many songbird species, young males learn their songs by imitating adult tutors. Biologist Ofer Tchernichovski found that zebra finches raised in isolation produced abnormal songs. When these isolated birds later became tutors themselves, their pupils learned the abnormal songs but modified them slightly toward the species' typical song. After three or four generations of tutoring, the songs of the descendants closely resembled those of wild zebra finches. These findings suggest that ______
Inferences.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: the typical zebra finch song results partly from learning biases that can reconstruct it even without an accurate model to copy.
zebra finches raised in isolation are unable to learn new songs from other birds, even when those birds are adults of their own species.
the songs of wild zebra finches have changed noticeably over the past several generations as birds have modified their tutors' songs.
young zebra finches prefer to learn from tutors whose songs most closely resemble the typical song of their species.

In spite of this,
Additionally,

Transitions.passage: The Dutch painter Judith Leyster was admired in her lifetime and became the first woman admitted to Haarlem's painters' guild. for example,
therefore,
in addition,

choices: however,
thus,
for instance,
likewise,
Transitions.expl: Oldingi gap: asalarilarga tayanish va xavotir. Keyingi: boshqa hasharotlar ham katta ulush qo'shadi — kutilganga nisbatan boshqacha manzara: 'however'. 'Thus' — natija emas. 'For instance' — misol emas, yangi burchak. 'Likewise' — o'xshashlik emas.

Specifically,
Moreover,

Transitions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

Nevertheless,
Similarly,
In comparison,

Rhetorical Synthesis.expl: Maqsad — oziq joylashuvini bildirish usullarini qarama-qarshi qo'yish. To'g'ri javob asalarilar raqsi (burchak va davomiylik) bilan ayrim nishsiz arilarning hid izlarini solishtiradi — ikkalasi ham joylashuv haqida. Uya ichidagi tovushlar haqidagi variant nozik tuzoq: tovush oziq sifatini bildiradi, joylashuvni emas. Faqat asalarilar yoki faqat nishsiz arilar haqidagi variantlarda taqqoslash yo'q.

While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• In 2004, the Kenyan environmentalist Wangari Maathai won the Nobel Peace Prize.
• She founded the Green Belt Movement in 1977.
• The movement has planted more than 51 million trees in Kenya.
• It paid rural women small sums to plant and care for seedlings.
• Maathai argued that environmental destruction contributed to poverty and conflict.
Rhetorical Synthesis.prompt: The student wants to explain how the Green Belt Movement linked environmental and economic goals. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: By paying rural women to plant and care for seedlings, the Green Belt Movement combined reforestation with a source of income.
Founded by Wangari Maathai in 1977, the Green Belt Movement has planted more than 51 million trees across Kenya in the decades since then.
Wangari Maathai, the Kenyan environmentalist who founded the Green Belt Movement in 1977, won the 2004 Nobel Peace Prize.
Wangari Maathai, founder of the Green Belt Movement, argued that environmental destruction contributed to conflict.
Rhetorical Synthesis.expl: Maqsad — harakat ekologik va iqtisodiy maqsadni qanday bog'laganini tushuntirish. To'g'ri javob: qishloq ayollariga ko'chat ekish va parvarishlash uchun haq to'langan — daraxt + daromad. Maathai 'environmental destruction contributed to conflict' degani haqidagi variant eng yaqin tuzoq, lekin iqtisodiy bog'lanish usulini ko'rsatmaydi. 51 million daraxt yoki Nobel mukofoti haqidagi variantlarda bog'lanish yo'q.

While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Mayan city of Tikal was a major urban center from about 200 to 900 CE.
• In 2018, researchers used lidar, a laser-based scanning technology, to survey the forest around Tikal.
• Lidar can detect structures hidden beneath dense vegetation.
• The survey revealed more than 60,000 previously unknown structures.
• The findings suggest the region's population was far larger than previously estimated.
Rhetorical Synthesis.prompt: The student wants to emphasize the significance of the 2018 survey's findings. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: The 2018 lidar survey around Tikal revealed more than 60,000 previously unknown structures, suggesting the region's population was far larger than once thought.
In 2018, researchers used lidar, a laser-based scanning technology that can detect structures hidden beneath dense vegetation, to survey Tikal.
The Mayan city of Tikal was a major urban center from about 200 to 900 CE, and in 2018 researchers surveyed the forest around it using lidar technology.
Using lidar, which can detect structures hidden beneath dense vegetation, researchers found more than 60,000 previously unknown structures around Tikal in 2018.
Rhetorical Synthesis.expl: Maqsad — topilmalar ahamiyati. To'g'ri javob nima topilganini (60 000 dan ortiq noma'lum inshoot) va u nimani anglatishini (aholi ancha ko'p bo'lgan) aytadi. Lidar texnologiyasini tushuntirgan yoki Tikal tarixini aytgan variantlar faqat tadqiqot o'tkazilganini aytadi; 60 000 inshootni aytib, aholi haqidagi xulosasiz qolgan variant ham ahamiyatni ochib bermaydi.

Rhetorical Synthesis.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Architect Zaha Hadid designed the Heydar Aliyev Center in Baku, Azerbaijan.
• The building opened in 2012.
• Its exterior has no straight lines; its surfaces flow in continuous curves.
• Hadid's earlier Vitra Fire Station (1993) in Germany is made of sharp, angular concrete planes.
• Hadid became the first woman to win the Pritzker Architecture Prize in 2004.
Rhetorical Synthesis.prompt: The student wants to highlight a difference between two of Hadid's buildings. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: Whereas Hadid's Vitra Fire Station is made of sharp, angular concrete planes, the exterior of her Heydar Aliyev Center flows in continuous curves.
Zaha Hadid designed both the Vitra Fire Station, completed in Germany in 1993, and the Heydar Aliyev Center, which opened in Azerbaijan in 2012.
The Heydar Aliyev Center in Baku, Azerbaijan, which opened in 2012, has an exterior with no straight lines at all, its surfaces flowing in smooth, continuous curves.
Zaha Hadid, who designed the Heydar Aliyev Center in Baku, was the first woman to win the Pritzker Architecture Prize, in 2004.
Rhetorical Synthesis.expl: Maqsad — ikki bino o'rtasidagi farq. To'g'ri javob Vitra o't o'chirish stansiyasining o'tkir, burchakli beton tekisliklarini Heydar Aliyev markazining uzluksiz egri chiziqlariga qarama-qarshi qo'yadi. Ikkala binoni yil va joy bilan sanagan variant farqni aytmaydi; faqat Boku binosi yoki Pritzker mukofoti haqidagi variantlarda taqqoslash yo'q.
